You are Engineer — the STANDING engineering teammate of the cavecrew tribe. Long-lived role: you persist across many tasks this session. Repo: /home/phili/tools/cavecrew-mcp (WSL). The tribe runs Minecraft bots via cave/runner.js (per-bot HTTP API on 127.0.0.1:3201+) + cave/skills.js (deterministic skills). LLM drivers drive bots; they log quirks/bugs into cave/FEEDBACK.md; team-lead (me) routes work to you.

YOUR CHARTER:
- You own the SMALL engineering work: quirk fixes off FEEDBACK.md, small endpoints, doc/registry syncs, test scripts. Bounded changes, typically 1-2 files.
- You TEST your own work: `node --check` minimum, plus targeted checks (grep call sites, dry-run scripts, tests/ where applicable). Never report done without a check actually run.
- BIG changes (multi-file features, subtle concurrency, deep refactors) are NOT yours solo — when a task smells big, say so to team-lead and recommend a Workflow instead; you may then get integration/verify slices of it.
- You COMMIT your own finished work locally: small focused commits, message style matches repo history (short SHOUTY-prefix summary + terse body). NEVER push — team-lead reviews and pushes.
- Report to team-lead via SendMessage when a task is done or blocked (if SendMessage is unavailable, your final text response serves as the report). Report caveman style: short, exact file:line refs, what checked.

ONBOARDING (do now):
1. Read cave/README.md, cave/DRIVER_GUIDE.md (API surface), cave/FEEDBACK.md (the quirk backlog — your future work feed), cave/CIV.md, cave/BASE.md. Skim cave/runner.js + cave/skills.js structure (don't deep-read everything, learn the map: endpoint table, task mutex, skills exports, zones/announce plumbing).
2. Check `git log --oneline -8` for today's context (leak fix, grove fix, idleguard endpoint just landed).
3. FIRST TASK — event-ring hygiene (from FEEDBACK entries "event ring flooded by FEL join/leave spam" + today's idle-guard 400+ retry-spam flood, see issue #6 comments):
   a. cave/runner.js pushEvent/ring: exclude foreign join/leave system messages from the ring (the "[FEL] X joined/left" class — other players' join/left lines, NOT our own bot's), and add a simple per-source rate cap so one spammy source (e.g. idle-guard deposit retries) cannot wipe the whole 500-entry ring in seconds (e.g. max ~30 entries per (type) per 60s window, drop + count suppressed, emit one "…suppressed N similar" entry when a window ends).
   b. While in there: idle-guard deposit-on-full-chest should back off — if deposit target chest reports full / deposit fails twice in a row, idle-guard skips further deposit attempts for 10 minutes (one log line, one ring entry). Grep the idle-guard cycle code (maybeStartIdleGuard / idleGuardCycle).
   c. `node --check cave/runner.js`, then commit (do not push, do not restart any runner — team-lead owns deploys; running bots keep old code until team-lead restarts them).
4. Report: map learned (3 bullets max), task 3 changes (file:line), checks run, commit hash.

Style note: all your user-visible reports in caveman style — short sentences, "me" for self — but code, paths, numbers EXACT.
</teammate-message>

# cave/

Standalone bot-fleet layer bolted onto this repo's mineflayer bot. Plain
ESM JavaScript, no TypeScript, no build step. Does not touch `src/` or
`dist/` — this repo's original MCP server keeps working untouched.

## Three-layer architecture

1. **Deterministic runner** (`runner.js` + `skills.js`) — one Node
   process per bot, connects to the Minecraft server via mineflayer, and
   exposes a small HTTP API on `127.0.0.1:<port>`. All the actually
   reliable behavior (chop a tree, mine a block, path to a point, deposit
   to a chest) lives here as plain algorithms, with known field quirks
   (re-equip tools per swing, snipe-proof drop collection, safe descents,
   etc.) encoded directly in the code rather than left to chance.
2. **LLM drivers** — one driver agent per bot, talking to that bot's HTTP
   API. Drivers decide *what* to do and narrate it in-game; the runner
   handles *how*. See `DRIVER_GUIDE.md` for the full API reference and
   conventions a driver must follow.
3. **Orchestrator** — coordinates drivers across the fleet, tracks tribe
   state in `CIV.md`, and is the one who updates `skills.js` when a
   driver reports a quirk that keeps tripping up the deterministic layer.

## Commands

Run from the repo root (`cavecrew-mcp/`):

```powershell
# start a bot — refuses if it's already running or the port is taken
node cave/spawn.mjs start UngaBunga 3201

# stop a bot — best-effort /stop, then kills the process tree
node cave/spawn.mjs stop UngaBunga

# list every bot with a pid file, and whether it's actually alive
node cave/spawn.mjs list
```

`spawn.mjs` never talks to Minecraft itself — it only manages the
`runner.js` OS processes (pid files in `cave/pids/`, logs in
`cave/logs/`, both gitignored). Once a bot is up, drive it over HTTP per
`DRIVER_GUIDE.md`.

## File map

| File               | What it is                                                |
|--------------------|------------------------------------------------------------|
| `runner.js`        | Per-bot process: mineflayer connection + HTTP task API.     |
| `skills.js`        | Deterministic algorithms the runner's endpoints call into.  |
| `spawn.mjs`        | CLI to start/stop/list bot processes.                       |
| `DRIVER_GUIDE.md`  | API reference and conventions for LLM driver agents.        |
| `CIV.md`           | Tribe state: naming scheme, port registry, roster, goals.   |
| `logs/`            | Per-bot log files (gitignored).                              |
| `pids/`            | Per-bot pid-file records used by `spawn.mjs` (gitignored).  |

addedLines: - cavecrew-builder: Bounded implementation worker — edits 1-2 files per task with exact instructions. Use for scoped edits, not open-ended features. Returns caveman-compressed report — ~60% fewer tokens into main context. (Tools: Read, Edit, Write, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- cavecrew-investigator: Locate code, trace symbols, map subsystems. Read-only hunter. Use instead of vanilla Explore when answer is "where is X / how does X flow". Returns caveman-compressed findings — ~60% fewer tokens into main context. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- cavecrew-reviewer: Diff review — correctness bugs, edge cases, dumb waste. Point at a diff, branch, or file set. Returns caveman-compressed findings ranked by severity — ~60% fewer tokens into main context. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)
- claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`; (5) `claude plugin eval` (writing and running plugin eval suites, its JSON/report, sandbox, CI, early-access enablement) and the `/skill-doctor` report. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

You DRAFT the design as .dc.html artboards laid out on one pan/zoom canvas; where saving is enabled for the user's account they refine every element visually (click-to-select, a properties panel, inline text editing, undo/redo) and Save publishes a new version for everyone, otherwise they get a view-and-export (PNG/PDF) preview of your draft. Good for UI mockups and screen flows, landing pages, marketing and social graphics, and print pieces - posters, flyers, brochures as single-page artboards; memos and reports as one flowing artboard. Use when someone wants a design, mockup, wireframe, UI or screen design, landing page, poster, flyer, brochure, banner, card, one-pager, or any visual layout they would rather tweak by hand than in code. Only for CREATING or re-seeding a canvas; an existing one is edited in its published Artifact.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, remembering what people do on it (a poll, a sign-up sheet, a checklist, a document edited in place — it saves new versions of itself), keeping state shared across viewers, knowing who is viewing, asking Claude a question of its own, storing files people add, or handing the viewer a file to save. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.

Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). # FEEDBACK.md — append-only quirk/bug/idea log (FEL-style learning loop)

Every driver logs each quirk/bug/idea THE MOMENT it is found. Engine work
cycles consume open entries. Format:

```
## [open|shipped] short-title — BotName, YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM
symptom / evidence / suggested fix
```

## [open] craft pocket-grid voids materials — Grog, 2026-09-01
/craft birch_planks ate 19 logs, made 4 torches, usedTable:false. FEL confirms:
2x2 pocket batch crafts VOID materials. Fix: ALWAYS craft at table (in flight).

## [open] pathfinder digs with held tool — FEL intel, 2026-09-01
Traversal digging uses currently held tool — long moves eat iron durability.
Fix: equip cheap/no tool before travel legs.

## [open] nuisance block wedges movement — FEL intel, 2026-09-01
Torch/leaf_litter in bot's own tile = path reported but no movement. Detect +
dig block underfoot when goto frozen.

## [open] bucket fill: activateBlock fails — FEL intel, 2026-09-01
Use lookAt(water) + bot.activateItem(), not activateBlock.

## [open] blockAt stale for unvisited chunks — FEL intel, 2026-09-01
Walk near before trusting scans.

## [open] Movements safety config — FEL intel (their fall death), 2026-09-01
Set allowParkour=false, maxDropDown=3, allow1by1towers=false,
allowSprinting=false, infiniteLiquidDropdownDistance=false, scafoldingBlocks=[].
Also stops ugly self-built dirt towers on landscape.

## [open] ledger lines must stay REAL white chat — FEL intel, 2026-09-01
tellraw system msgs don't fire chat events — other bots parse DEPOT/TRADE/USING
lines from real chat. Grey wiring must EXCLUDE protocol-prefixed lines
(DEPOT |TRADE |USING |FREE |LEASE-BREAK |BASE |CLAIM |HELLO |OFFER ).
UPDATE 2026-09-01 (chief decree, DEPOT DE-CHAT): DEPOT is EXEMPTED from this
rule and removed from runner.js's PROTOCOL_PREFIX — depot lines are our own
bookkeeping, not an inter-tribe protocol, and they now route to the Discord
status feed via announce('status'). Every other prefix above is unchanged and
still enforced. Drivers keep sending DEPOT lines via /chat as before, format
unchanged. Known consequence: cave/scoreboard.mjs parses "DEPOT " out of the
server latest.log CHAT lines only, so its depot accounting goes silent until
repointed at the new feed.

## [open] health<8 panic listener at game speed — FEL intel, 2026-09-01
Injected health listener: abort task, announce, flee home — BUT when deep/far,
wall off line-of-sight with cobble + eat instead. Game-speed reflex, not LLM.

## [open] torch kit rule — FEL intel (their 3 deaths in dark pockets), 2026-09-01
Every bot carries ≥8 torches on excursions, lights workspace ~7 spacing.
Deep kit below y0: 40 torches, armor, 2 picks, 8 food, durability tracking.

## [open] sign placement via bot fails (blockUpdate timeout) — UngaBunga, 2026-09-01
Orchestrator RCON setblock works; bot-side placeSign needs investigation.

## [open] setControlState no-op without preceding bot.look() — Thak, 2026-09-01 06:40
CONFIRMED reproducible: bare bot.setControlState("jump",true) (or "forward") in
eval produced ZERO position/velocity change for 3+ consecutive full test batches
(fixed-sleep AND polling-wait variants both failed identically, ruling out
timing) — velocity.y stuck at passive gravity tick (-0.0784) the whole hold
window, onGround never left true. Root cause isolated: NOT a "wedge"/stuck-bot
state (this was NOT the nuisance-tile bug — target tile was already clean air).
Adding a single bot.look(bot.entity.yaw,0,true) call immediately before the
setControlState toggle made jump AND forward work correctly every time after,
in the same session, same bot, same spot. Suspect: control-state changes get
silently dropped by the client tick loop until a look/position packet is sent
to "wake" it, possibly after any prior eval task leaves controls idle for a
stretch. Fix: ALWAYS call bot.look(bot.entity.yaw, bot.entity.pitch, true)
immediately before setControlState-driven movement in any eval script. This
likely explains some/all of the earlier "movement wedge" reports this session
that tp+restart "fixed" — restart implicitly re-establishes look state too.

## [open] placeBlock uses currently-held item, not a smart pick — Thak, 2026-09-01 06:40
Pillar-climb loop's placeBlock calls kept failing with "Event blockUpdate did
not fire within timeout of 5000ms" against a perfectly valid solid reference
block. Ground-truth check (bot.heldItem) showed bot was holding a TORCH (left
over from earlier route-marking) — bot.placeBlock places whatever is equipped,
it does NOT auto-select a sensible building block. Compounding gotcha: a torch
sitting in a tile reports boundingBox:"empty" (correctly, for movement/pathing
purposes) but STILL occupies the tile for block-placement purposes, so a
naive "only dig if boundingBox==='block'" clearance check misses it entirely —
must instead check block.name!=="air" when clearing a placement target. Fix
for any place/build skill: explicitly bot.equip(desiredBlockItem,"hand")
right before every placeBlock call, and clear target tiles by name!=="air",
not by boundingBox.

## [open] mine/collect wedge-detector false-positives on tight ore pockets — Thak, 2026-09-01 06:52
Both a /mine and a /collect task failed back-to-back with the runner's own
"wedge: zero progress over 90s ... likely wedged; escalate per stuck-taxonomy"
error, at the exact spot a coal_ore vein had just been dug out. Ground-truth
check (blockAt scan of the 3x3 column around feet) showed the real cause each
time: the bot was simply sealed in a 1x1 mined-out pocket — every horizontal
neighbor at foot level solid, nothing to move "forward" into regardless of
facing. This is a normal, expected end-state after digging an ore vein, NOT
an engine wedge. Manually digging one side wall free (bot.dig on the block at
feet.offset(-1,0,0) toward whichever neighbor cell has head-height clearance)
and walking out worked instantly both times — no tp/restart needed. The
runner's stuck-taxonomy escalation ladder is overkill for this case and wastes
90s + a task failure per occurrence. Suggest: before declaring a wedge, have
mine/collect check whether ALL 4 horizontal foot-level neighbors are solid
(self-dug-in pocket) and auto-dig one exit before falling through to the
raw-control-test/tp+restart ladder — same fix likely helps buildStaircase too.

## [open] genuine movement wedge, look-fix + relog both failed — Thak, 2026-09-01 07:11
Distinct from the two "wedge" entries above (which were both false positives —
tight ore pocket and diagonal corner-cut). This one is real: at (11,86,55),
directly below chest A, bare bot.look()+forward-alone produced velocity.x/z
exactly 0, isCollidedHorizontally:false, feet tile confirmed clean air (no
nuisance block), onGround:true — everything structurally normal, just zero
control response. Tried /relog per the standard ladder: reconnected fine but
did NOT clear the freeze (identical zero-velocity result immediately after).
Escalated to team-lead for tp+restart (the one thing that reliably cleared
this class of wedge earlier in the session). Also flagging as a possible
correlated cause: this exact spot had a 100% (20/20) placeBlock failure rate
moments before the freeze, right in the column under chest A/camp footprint,
after normal partial-success rates everywhere else in open cave this session —
worth checking whether a region-protection plugin around camp is involved in
both the placement wall and this freeze.

## [open] toss self-repickup — UngaBunga, 2026-08-31
bot.toss reports ok but bot re-grabs own drop; toss + walk 3 back (giveItems
helper in flight).

## [open] pf engine "goal changed" false-fail on short hops — UngaBunga, 2026-09-01
gotoLoopPf failed twice in a row on a ~1-2 block hop right after the blink
restart ("The goal was changed before it could be completed!"), bot barely
moved. Same target with engine:"ash" worked first try. Also hit inside
/deposit (which always uses pf internally, no engine param) — worked around
by skipping gotoChestBlock entirely and calling bot.openChest directly via
/eval once already in range. Suggest: let /deposit and /withdraw accept an
engine override, or default their internal goto to ash post-blink.

## [open] event ring flooded by FEL join/leave spam — useless for forensics — team-lead, 2026-09-01
Ook's ring at seq 10k+: nearly every entry = "[FEL] X joined/left the game"
(their reconnect storms). Task/error events drowned out — could not
reconstruct a task-replacement sequence. Fix: exclude foreign join/leave
system messages from the ring (or keep a separate task-only ring). Cheap,
high forensic value.

## [open] UPDATE on "force task silently replaced": may be TWO-COMMANDERS problem — team-lead, 2026-09-01
New data: my forced goto on Ook (task-8, accepted, running) was replaced
within 45s by a hunt task — but OokDriver was simultaneously running his own
meat-run chain. The Durk/Mog cases also had drivers issuing their own
force-gotos around the same window. So "idle-guard eats tasks" may really be
"orchestrator and driver both command the same bot" — last write wins, each
side sees its task vanish. DOCTRINE FIX adopted now: ONE commander per bot —
driver owns the bot while active; orchestrator pushes only to bots with
idle/absent drivers, and messages the driver instead when active. Code-side:
arbitration check still worthwhile (a task-source field on tasks — driver vs
orchestrator vs idle-guard — logged per replacement would settle this
forever).

## [open] goto false-reach reports IDENTICAL stale distance from different positions — Grog, 2026-09-01
pf goto false-reach check reported the EXACT same "9.30 blocks horiz / 3.00
vert" on two separate attempts from two DIFFERENT actual positions — cannot
be a live measurement. Looks like the distance in the false-reach error is
computed from a stale/cached position (or the goal snapshot) rather than
bot.entity.position at check time. Separate from the known 1.80 constant-gap
bug (that one is fixed). Check goalGroundTruth's position source in
movement.js. Workaround that worked: short pf hops instead of one long goto.

## [open] chopTrees root cause: ensureTool axe-craft-chain wedges bare-handed — UngaBunga, 2026-09-01
Follow-up to the entry below with the real signature, from a watched
count:1 test: task failed at detail "ensureTool: craft chain for axe",
error "wedge: zero progress over 90s (no ite[ms gained?])". Reproduced with
zero logs/planks/sticks/axe in inventory, no crafting table or depot chest
within reach (90+ blocks out in the south wood zone). Looks like the
craft-chain has nothing to bootstrap the very first log from and just sits
waiting rather than punching one bare-handed. Suggest: ensureTool's axe
chain should try one bare-hand log punch first when totally bare, before
falling back to table/depot logic.

## [open] ROOT CAUSE of chop deaths: ensureTool axe craft-chain wedges when totally bare — UngaBunga, 2026-09-01
Trace test (count:1 chop, live watch): task died at detail "ensureTool: craft
chain for axe" with wedge-watchdog error "zero progress over 90s". NOT a
chopTrees stall — ensureTool's craft chain deadlocks when the bot holds ZERO
log/plank/stick AND no table AND no depot chest in reach (bare kit, 90+
blocks from camp = exact setup on every dead run). It waits for materials
nothing will ever produce. Fix: when fully bare-handed far from base,
ensureTool must BOOTSTRAP — punch ONE log bare-hand first (slow but
guaranteed), then table→sticks→axe. Watchdog worked perfectly here (loud
fail instead of eternal running). Supersedes/refines the "chopTrees dies
with stalled" entry below.

## [open] chopTrees dies with "stalled" mid-tree, no auto-retry — UngaBunga, 2026-09-01
/chop task failed outright with result.error:"stalled" while at "chopping
tree 1/12" (south wood zone, z=109, well clear of camp). Bot did not
recover on its own; sat at idle-guard cycling with zero logs gained until
team-lead force-pushed a fresh /chop. No world hazard (health/food both 20,
open ground) — looks like an internal watchdog inside chopTrees giving up
rather than retrying the current tree or moving to the next one. Suggest:

mistake on my part. Fix: replant EACH tile immediately after digging it,
same visit, before moving off it for collect — don't batch dig-all then
collect-then-replant across the whole plot. If batching digs is still
wanted for efficiency, at minimum route the post-harvest /collect so it

## [open] 2X CONFIRMED: idle-guard sweeps driver's KEEP items + retry-spam floods event ring — Grog, 2026-09-01 09:13/09:19
Left Grog idle ~90s (reading a teammate msg, no task issued) between task-10 and task-11. Runner's
built-in idle-guard fired its default "deposit toward chest A" and dumped almost the WHOLE
inventory in one pass — including crafting_table, bread x5, and BOTH furnace x2 — items the driver
was explicitly told to KEEP on the bot, not bank. No keep-list/allowlist concept exists in
idle-guard's deposit path; it deposits everything non-tool, full stop. Recovered by withdrawing
them back afterward (worked fine), but if idle-guard had fired mid-task instead of at a clean idle
point, or if the driver hadn't caught it, kit loss was real (had it been food during a fight, or a
tool needed same-session, this bites harder than lost chest slots).

Second, worse finding: once chest A hit its 27-slot cap partway through the sweep, idle-guard did
NOT stop or back off — it kept cycling (`detail:"idle-guard: cycle 66"` through at least `"cycle
97"` observed, 31+ cycles in under 30s) re-attempting the SAME failed items (oak_door, oak_log,
diorite, andesite, dripstone_block, birch_planks, birch_sapling, raw_copper, apple,
pointed_dripstone) every cycle, each retry logging one `quirk depositToChest: failed to deposit
X: destination full` event PER ITEM. This produced 400+ ring events in under a minute (confirmed:
/events?since=34 right after had already rolled seq past 1150, vs. seq 35 before idle-guard fired)
— blew this bot's entire session history (task-1..task-10, the sethome/goto/bank steps) straight
out of the 500-entry ring before I could reference it. Same disease as the already-logged "event
ring flooded by FEL join/leave spam" entry above, different source (own idle-guard retry-loop
instead of foreign join/leave spam) — both point at the same fix: notable-task-events need their
own ring, or spam-dedup on repeated identical quirk lines within a short window.

Suggest: (1) idle-guard's default-deposit should accept/consult a driver-set keep-list (or at
minimum a "keep last N food + first crafting_table + first furnace" heuristic) before sweeping;
(2) idle-guard should back off (stop retrying, or drop to a single warning) the moment ANY item in
its batch reports "destination full" instead of full-speed-retrying the identical failing batch
every cycle; (3) ring buffer should either dedup identical consecutive quirk lines or keep a
separate task-only ring, so one spam episode can't erase real task history.

UPDATE 09:19Z — RECURRED, same session, ~6 min later: after I'd already withdrawn crafting_table 1
+ furnace 1 (spare) + cobblestone 16 back onto Grog per team-lead's explicit keep-list, another
idle gap (reading/processing a teammate message, no bot task issued) let idle-guard fire a THIRD
time and re-deposit all three straight back into chest A — this time pushing chest A to a hard
27/27 slots FULL (confirmed via containerItems().length). Recovered again (partial-count eval
withdraw), chest back to 26/27. Two-for-two: every idle gap this session that lasted through a
message-processing pause triggered a sweep, 100% hit rate, and the second occurrence had a real
consequence (drove a shared depot chest to capacity) rather than just noise. This is not a rare
edge case, it's the default outcome of any driver pause long enough to read+act on a teammate
message — strongly reinforces fix (1) above (keep-list) as high priority, not a nice-to-have.

1	# DRIVER_GUIDE.md — for LLM driver agents
2	
3	You are driving one cavecrew bot through its runner's HTTP API. The runner
4	(`cave/runner.js`) holds the deterministic loop, the pathfinding, and the
5	field-quirk workarounds — your job is to issue tasks, watch them resolve,
6	narrate what's happening in-game, and use judgment when the deterministic
7	skills aren't enough. Check `CIV.md` for the port registry and roster
8	before you start: it tells you which port your bot's API is on.
9	
10	All examples below use `curl.exe` from Windows PowerShell (the `.exe`
11	suffix matters — plain `curl` is a PowerShell alias for
12	`Invoke-WebRequest` and does not behave the same way). Replace `3201`
13	with your bot's actual port from `CIV.md`.
14	
15	## Poll discipline — read this first
16	
17	- **Single-poll contract**: every task response from `/status` carries
18	  its own state and result. You do not need to chain calls — one
19	  `/status` poll tells you everything about the current task.
20	- **Poll every 15-30 seconds** while a task is running. Do not poll
21	  faster than that — you will flood the runner and the log for no
22	  benefit. A `chop` or `mine` task can legitimately take a couple of
23	  minutes.
24	- **One task at a time.** The runner enforces a single-task mutex: if you
25	  POST a new task while one is already running, you get back `409
26	  {"error":"busy","currentTask":{...}}`. Either wait for the current task
27	  to finish, POST `/stop` to cancel it, or add `"force": true` to the new
28	  request body to cancel-then-start.
29	- Never spam-loop `/eval` or `/status`. If you're unsure what's
30	  happening, one `/status` call answers it.
31	
32	## Escalation rule
33	
34	If a deterministic skill (`/chop`, `/mine`, `/goto`, etc.) **fails twice
35	in a row on the same objective**, stop retrying it as-is. Instead:
36	
37	1. Drop to `/eval` and reason through the problem manually (see below).
38	2. **Report the quirk to the orchestrator** — what you were trying to do,
39	   what actually happened, and what worked instead — so it gets coded
40	   into `skills.js` as a permanent fix. A quirk you work around by hand
41	   and don't report will bite the next bot too.
42	
43	## Narration
44	
45	Narrate every phase of what you're doing **in-game, in English, via
46	`/chat`** — not just in your own reasoning. Other players (and other
47	cavecrew bots) should be able to follow along from chat alone: "heading
48	out to chop wood", "found a cave, mining down", "under attack, falling
49	back". Keep lines short.
50	
51	## Conduct rules
52	
53	- **Never attack players.** `/hunt` only ever targets passive mobs by
54	  design, but this also applies to anything you do through `/eval` — no
55	  player-targeting, ever, for any reason.
56	- **Never touch the other tribe's chests or builds.** The other tribe on
57	  this server is **FurzFriedrich, MettMarcel, BuddelBernd, KackboonKevin**.
58	  Their chest depot near the crafting-table cluster around
59	  **(-3, 111, 4)** is **theirs** — do not open, deposit to, withdraw
60	  from, or break anything there or anywhere else that looks like their
61	  build. When in doubt, back off and ask in chat rather than guess.
62	- **Never leave drops on the ground.** Skills already collect
63	  immediately after felling/mining (rival bots snipe drops within
64	  seconds) — if you do anything through `/eval` that drops items, follow
65	  up with `/collect` before moving on. **Standing law: after every
66	  chop/mine/hunt task, run `/collect {"radius":24}`** as a sweep — 24
67	  blocks, not the 16 default, so nothing gets left for rivals.
68	- **Protected blocks — never dug by skills.** `safeDig` (the one
69	  choke point every `/chop`, `/mine`, `/staircase`, `/branchmine`, etc.
70	  dig goes through) refuses outright to dig chests, barrels, furnaces,
71	  crafting tables, beds, anvils, enchanting tables, brewing stands,
72	  lecterns, composters, or signs — by block **type**, fleet-wide, no
73	  coordinate list to keep in sync. This is a hard stop, not a skip: a
74	  task that walks into one of these gets an error, not a silent detour.
75	  If you need to actually remove one of our own fixtures on purpose, do
76	  it through `/eval` directly, not through the deterministic skills.
77	- **Wedge-detection.** If a `/goto` (or any skill built on it) fails
78	  every retry attempt while a nuisance block — a torch, leaf_litter,
79	  short_grass, or snow layer — is sitting in the bot's own foot/head
80	  tile, the skill layer digs just that one block and retries once before
81	  giving up for real. Travel itself never auto-digs (see Depth law and
82	  the Movements note below), so a bot wedged on its own just-placed
83	  torch used to just fail; now it self-clears the narrow, pre-vetted
84	  nuisance set on its own. That set is ONLY those four zero-collision
85	  block types — never fences, walls, slabs, stairs, carpets, or anything
86	  else a build could be made of. If a task still fails after that, the
87	  block in the way genuinely isn't on the safe-to-clear list — report it
88	  per the Escalation rule rather than manually digging around it via
89	  `/eval`.
90	- **Best tool always equipped.** The skills layer re-equips the correct
91	  tool before every dig — you don't need to manage this yourself when
92	  using `/chop`, `/mine`, etc. If you're doing manual digging through
93	  `/eval`, equip the right tool first.
94	- **Idle & nag law (two-tier).** If your bot has been idle (no running
95	  task) for more than **60 seconds**, that's a bug in your loop, not a
96	  rest break — self-issue the next step from the goal ladder in `CIV.md`
97	  or your workstation assignment (see Anti-clump below) immediately,
98	  don't wait to be asked. Separately, if **you as a driver** have gone
99	  quiet — no `/status` poll, no `/chat` narration, nothing — for **5+
100	  minutes**, that's nag-worthy: the senior driver / team-lead should ping
101	  you, and if you're the one who notices another driver has gone quiet
102	  that long, ping them. The two timers are independent: a bot can be
103	  correctly mid-task (not idle) while its driver is still expected to be
104	  actively polling/narrating, not silent for 5+ minutes.
105	- **Anti-clump — per-bot workstations.** Each bot has a home working area
106	  so the crew spreads out instead of stacking on one spot:
107	  Grog = house site (20, 89, 58); UngaBunga = trading post ~(3, 95, 22);
108	  Thak = mine field (24, 90, 64); Bonk = door staging (10, 90, 61);
109	  Zug = farm (8-11, 58-59). When your goal doesn't pin you elsewhere,
110	  default back to your own workstation rather than following the crowd.
111	  If you notice multiple bots stacked on the same block with no shared
112	  task reason, that's the anti-clump law being violated — one of you
113	  should move.
114	- **Watching ≠ working.** Standing near another bot while it does
115	  something is not itself work, and doesn't exempt your bot from the
116	  idle law above. If you're not issuing your own task, you're idle — act
117	  accordingly (self-issue the next step) even if the scene looks busy
118	  because a neighbor bot is active.
119	- **Ground-truth verify.** Before reporting a step "done" — in chat, to
120	  the team-lead, or in a doc update — confirm it against actual state
121	  (`/status`, `/eval` reading real inventory/position/blocks), not
122	  against your own or another bot's chat narration. Narration can lag or
123	  be wrong; the world state via the API is the source of truth.
124	- **Equality doctrine.** All five bots are equally cavecrew. No bot's
125	  task, goal, or driver outranks another's by default — conflicts (e.g.
126	  two bots wanting the same resource/spot) get resolved by the team-lead,
127	  not by whichever bot claims priority first.
128	- **Depth law — SOLVED.** `buildStaircase` and `branchMine` are both live
129	  on the runner (see below). Deep ore goes through that pair only. Do not
130	  `/mine` raw ore more than **4 blocks below your own feet** by hand —
131	  that's how bots fall into ravines and lava pockets. Staircase down
132	  properly first.
133	- **Trade etiquette.** If another player (especially the neighbor tribe)
134	  offers a trade, only ever take the items they actually offered — never
135	  grab extra out of an open chest or inventory. Send a `DEPOT`-style
136	  chat line recording what was traded so it's auditable. Compliments in
137	  chat go over well with **KackboonKevin** specifically — a friendly
138	  line costs nothing and has smoothed past interactions.
139	- **Trading post protocol.** Full trading-post layout (chest positions,
140	  which chest is CAVE's vs FEL's, the `TRADE take X leave Y` chat-line
141	  format) lives in `TRADE.md` — read it before driving any trade-post
142	  task, don't improvise the protocol from this file alone.
143	- **tp-rescue policy — SUPERSEDED.** Orchestrator/RCON `/tp` rescues are
144	  now **BANNED**. See "HOME SYSTEM (self-rescue)" below — a stuck bot
145	  runs `/trigger home` on itself instead of waiting for an admin
146	  teleport. `/goto` remains the tool for everything routine; report the
147	  stuck condition per the escalation rule so the underlying pathing bug
148	  gets fixed regardless of how the bot recovered.
149	- **Blink protocol.** A bot that visibly teleports/snaps position in
150	  chat or logs without a `/tp` rescue in play (position jump with no
151	  corresponding `/goto` completion or death) is "blinking" — treat it as
152	  a connection/desync symptom, not normal movement. Check `/status` for
153	  `connected: true` and a sane `pos`, and `/relog` if anything looks off,
154	  per the Disconnect protocol below.
155	- **Plugin-first doctrine.** Prefer a maintained mineflayer plugin over
156	  hand-rolled `/eval` logic whenever one exists for what you need
157	  (pathfinding, auto-eat, web-inventory, etc.) — plugins are vetted once
158	  and reused, hand-rolled `/eval` code is a one-off that has to be
159	  re-derived and re-debugged every time. Reach for `/eval` only when no
160	  plugin covers the need, per the Escalation rule above.
161	- **Build standards.** When constructing camp structures (walls, roofs,
162	  staging), follow the established look: **log pillars** at corners,
163	  **plank infill** for walls, **windows** left as gaps (or glass if
164	  available) rather than solid walls throughout, and a **rimmed roof**
165	  (roof edge one block higher than the field, like a lip) rather than a
166	  flat plane. Matches the style UngaBunga used for the original camp
167	  shelter (now removed — see `CIV.md` state refresh — but the standard
168	  still applies to any rebuild).
169	- **Signs-for-labeling law.** Label camp fixtures — chests, crafting
170	  tables, staging areas — with a physical oak_sign where placement
171	  actually works. Where sign placement fails (see the sign-on-chest
172	  quirk logged in `CIV.md` under Trading post — `blockUpdate` timeout,
173	  target block stays `air`), fall back to chat + a note in `CIV.md`/
174	  `TRADE.md` instead of retrying indefinitely; report the placement
175	  failure per the escalation rule so it gets a real fix.
176	- **Chat tiers (grey / white / rainbow) — now auto-classified.** The
177	  default `/chat` style (`"talk"`, or no `style` at all) routes through
178	  the runner's `smartChat`: a line starting with `!` is stripped of the
179	  `!` and sent as **important white** real chat; a line starting with a
180	  protocol-ledger prefix (`TRADE `, `USING `, `FREE `,
181	  `LEASE-BREAK `, `BASE `, `CLAIM `, `HELLO `, `OFFER `) is sent
182	  **verbatim as real white chat**, unchanged, because other bots/tribes
183	  parse chat for those exact prefixes; everything else becomes **grey**
184	  routine narration automatically. You don't need to pick a style for
185	  ordinary narration ("heading out to chop wood") or for a DEPOT ledger
186	  line — just `/chat` it and the classification happens for you. Use
187	  `"style":"status"` to force grey regardless of content, or
188	  `"style":"rainbow"` for tribe-wide proclamations (a goal-ladder
189	  milestone, a new pact like the trading post no-touch exception).
190	- **DEPOT is no longer a white-chat prefix (chief, 2026-09-01).** `DEPOT `
191	  was removed from the protocol-ledger list above: depot lines are our own
192	  bookkeeping, not an inter-tribe protocol, and at fleet scale they were the
193	  loudest thing in public chat. They now classify as ordinary narration, so
194	  they ride the **Discord status feed** (grey in-game) instead. Nothing
195	  changes for you as a driver — keep sending `DEPOT` lines through `/chat`
196	  exactly as documented below; only the destination moved. Every other
197	  ledger prefix still goes out as real white chat, unchanged.
198	
199	## DEPOT ledger
200	
201	Once cavecrew has its own chests (goal ladder step 6 in `CIV.md`), every
202	deposit or withdrawal against a cavecrew chest gets a ledger line so the
203	whole tribe can follow the ledger.
204	
205	> **2026-09-01 (chief):** these lines go to the **Discord status feed**, not
206	> public white chat — see the DEPOT de-chat note under Chat tiers above. You
207	> still send them the same way (`/chat`, format unchanged); the runner
208	> classifies and routes them.
209	
210	```
211	DEPOT +N item (chest X)
212	DEPOT -N item (chest X)
213	```
214	
215	`N` is the count, `item` the item name, `X` identifies which chest (a
216	short label or coordinate). Example:
217	
218	```
219	DEPOT +64 cobblestone (chest A)
220	DEPOT -8 iron_ingot (chest A)
221	```
222	
223	Send this line via `/chat` yourself right after a `/deposit` or
224	`/withdraw` call succeeds.
225	
226	## Panic reflex (automatic)
227	
228	The runner watches health at game-packet speed, not driver-poll speed:
229	if health drops below **8**, it fires automatically — no `/chat` or
230	`/stop` from you required. It aborts the current task, announces
231	`!HP <n>/20 - breaking off, reacting to danger!` (real white chat), and
232	then either **flees to camp** (if reasonably close and shallow) or
233	**seals itself in place and eats** (if far from camp or deep below it —
234	a blind flee across unknown terrain is riskier than holing up). This is
235	debounced 30s so it won't refire on every low-health tick. Check
236	`/events` for a `panic` entry and `/status` afterward — the panic
237	response runs as a normal task (`kind: "panic-response"`), so it shows
238	up like anything else. Treat a panic firing as a real incident worth a
239	`/status` check and a chat narration of what you find, same as any other
240	unexpected task failure.
241	
242	## Death protocol
243	
244	- A death **aborts the current task** — whatever was running is over,
245	  don't assume it resumes on respawn.
246	- `GET /status` carries a `deathCount` field. Check it after any
247	  unexpected task failure or gap in `/events` — a jump means the bot
248	  died and respawned since you last looked.
249	- After a death, if the bot lost its kit (tools/armor), run a `/recover`
250	  kit run: get back to camp/depot, `ensureTool` (see below) the essentials
251	  back into hand, and only then resume the goal you were on.
252	- Poisoned targets (mobs/blocks flagged poisonous by the runner) are
253	  **auto-skipped** by the skills layer — you don't need to detect these
254	  yourself, but don't fight the skip by manually targeting them through
255	  `/eval`.
256	
257	## Disconnect protocol
258	
259	- If the bot has dropped off the server, endpoints return **503** while
260	  it's offline — that's the signal, not a bug to route around.
261	- First aid: `POST /relog` (reconnects the bot). Try this before
262	  anything else.
263	- If `/relog` doesn't bring it back and you hit a **second** disconnect
264	  in the same session, **report it** to the team-lead rather than
265	  looping `/relog` indefinitely — two disconnects in a row usually means
266	  something upstream (server restart, kick, crash) that a driver can't
267	  fix alone.
268	
269	## Structured mining (buildStaircase → branchMine)
270	
271	This pair of skills is **live on the runner** — the depth law is solved.
272	This is the required pattern for any real ore run.
273	
274	1. `POST /buildStaircase` to descend safely to target depth (torches +
275	   safe steps, not a raw dig-down).
276	2. `POST /branchMine` from the bottom of the staircase to sweep ore
277	   bands at that depth (branches off a central shaft, standard
278	   strip-mining pattern).
279	3. Only fall back to plain `/mine` for shallow, surface-adjacent blocks
280	   — not for anything past the 4-block depth law above.
281	
282	Exact body shapes for `/buildStaircase` and `/branchMine` — check
283	`/status` or ask the team-lead if the runner's response shape isn't
284	obvious from a first call; document what you learn back to `CIV.md` or
285	`skills.js` per the escalation rule.
286	
287	## ensureTool (auto tool chain)
288	
289	Skills that need a specific tool call `ensureTool` internally. When your
290	bot's inventory doesn't have the right tool:
291	
292	1. It checks current inventory first — no wasted trip if you already
293	   have it.
294	2. If missing, it goes to the depot at **(11, 89, 55)** and withdraws
295	   the tool if the chest has one — sends the `DEPOT -N item (chest X)`
296	   ledger line for you.
297	3. If the depot doesn't have it either, it walks the **craft chain**:
298	   gather/withdraw materials → craft table if needed → craft the tool.
299	
300	You don't need to drive this by hand — it's automatic inside `/chop`,
301	`/mine`, `/buildStaircase`, `/branchMine`, etc. Just expect a task to
302	take longer than usual the first time a bot needs a new tool tier.
303	
304	## placeBlock — slow confirm
305	
306	`placeBlock` (used internally by staircase/shelter skills, and via
307	`/eval` if you call it directly) confirms placement **slowly** — the
308	runner waits for the block-update packet before considering it done
309	rather than assuming success the instant the packet is sent. Don't treat
310	a pause here as a hang; give it a few extra seconds before you decide
311	something's wrong and escalate.
312	
313	## Team tags
314	
315	Each bot is on its own colored in-game team, named `cave_<name>` (e.g.
316	`cave_Grog`, `cave_UngaBunga`, `cave_Zug`), with chat prefixed `[CAVE]`
317	so tribe members are visually distinguishable from the neighbor tribe at
318	a glance. When a **new bot** joins the roster, it needs its team created
319	and joined via RCON before it's doing real work:
320	
321	```powershell
322	node swarm\rcon.mjs "team add cave_<Name>"
323	node swarm\rcon.mjs "team join cave_<Name> <Name>"
324	```
325	
326	Run these from `C:\Users\phili\tools\minecraft-mcp-v2`. Add the new
327	bot's name and port to the roster table in `CIV.md` at the same time.
328	
329	## Engine choice on `/goto`
330	
331	`engine` on `/goto` currently defaults to the runner's own pick (see
332	`GET /status`'s `"engine"` field) but you can force it: `"pf"`
333	(pathfinder) or `"ash"` (ashfinder). As of now, **`pf` is measured
334	faster on open ground** — prefer it for camp-to-camp or surface travel.
335	`ash` remains an option worth trying for tight cave/underground
336	navigation where pathfinder struggles. A proper safety A/B between the
337	two engines is **pending** — don't treat either as fully vetted yet, and
338	report any stuck/unsafe pathing back per the escalation rule regardless
339	of which engine you used.
340	
341	## API reference
342	
343	Base URL for every endpoint: `http://127.0.0.1:<port>` — bind is
344	loopback-only, this is not reachable off the machine.
345	
346	### `GET /status`
347	
348	Poll this to check on the current (or last) task and vitals.
349	
350	```powershell
351	curl.exe -s http://127.0.0.1:3201/status
352	```
353	
354	Response shape:
355	
356	```json
357	{
358	  "name": "UngaBunga",
359	  "connected": true,
360	  "pos": { "x": 12.5, "y": 64, "z": -8.1 },
361	  "health": 20,
362	  "food": 18,
363	  "gamemode": "survival",
364	  "inventory": [{ "name": "oak_log", "count": 6 }],
365	  "currentTask": {
366	    "id": "task-17",
367	    "kind": "chop",
368	    "state": "running",
369	    "detail": "chopping tree 3/8",
370	    "result": null
371	  },
372	  "lastError": null,
373	  "engine": "auto"
374	}
375	```
376	
377	`currentTask.state` is one of `running`, `done`, `failed`. `result`
378	carries the task's return value once it's `done`, or a failure summary
379	once `failed`.
380	
381	### `POST /goto`
382	
383	Looping goto — re-issues the pathfinder goal internally up to 5 times on
384	timeout before giving up. You don't need to retry this yourself.
385	
386	```powershell
387	curl.exe -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3201/goto `
388	  -H "Content-Type: application/json" `
389	  -d '{"x":100,"y":64,"z":-40,"range":1,"timeoutMs":45000}'
390	```
391	
392	Body: `{x, y, z, range?=1, timeoutMs?=45000, engine?}`. `engine` is
393	optional — `"auto"` (tries ashfinder, falls back to pathfinder), `"ash"`
394	(ashfinder only), or `"pf"` (pathfinder only). Omit it to use the runner's
395	own default (see `GET /status`'s `"engine"` field).
396	
397	### `POST /chop`
398	
399	```powershell
400	curl.exe -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3201/chop `
401	  -H "Content-Type: application/json" `
402	  -d '{"count":8,"maxDistance":48}'
403	```
404	
405	Body: `{count?=8, maxDistance?=48}`.
406	
407	### `POST /mine`
408	
409	```powershell
410	curl.exe -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3201/mine `
411	  -H "Content-Type: application/json" `
412	  -d '{"block":"stone","count":16,"maxDistance":48}'
413	```
414	
415	Body: `{block, count?=8, maxDistance?=48}`.
416	
417	### `POST /collect`
418	
419	```powershell
420	curl.exe -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3201/collect `
421	  -H "Content-Type: application/json" `
422	  -d '{"radius":16}'
423	```
424	
425	Body: `{radius?=16}`.
426	
427	### `POST /hunt`
428	
429	Passive mobs only — never players.
430	
431	```powershell
432	curl.exe -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3201/hunt `
433	  -H "Content-Type: application/json" `
434	  -d '{"mob":"cow","count":2}'
435	```
436	
437	Body: `{mob, count?=1}`.
438	
439	### `POST /follow`
440	
441	```powershell
442	curl.exe -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3201/follow `
443	  -H "Content-Type: application/json" `
444	  -d '{"player":"SomePlayer","range":3}'
445	```
446	
447	Body: `{player, range?=3}`.
448	
449	### `POST /deposit`
450	
451	```powershell
452	curl.exe -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3201/deposit `
453	  -H "Content-Type: application/json" `
454	  -d '{"x":10,"y":65,"z":20,"items":["cobblestone"]}'
455	```
456	
457	Body: `{x, y, z, items?}` — omit `items` to deposit everything except
458	tools. Send a `DEPOT +N item (chest X)` chat line per item afterward.
459	
460	### `POST /withdraw`
461	
462	```powershell
463	curl.exe -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3201/withdraw `
464	  -H "Content-Type: application/json" `
465	  -d '{"x":10,"y":65,"z":20,"items":["iron_ingot"]}'
466	```
467	
468	Body: `{x, y, z, items}`. Send a `DEPOT -N item (chest X)` chat line per
469	item afterward.
470	
471	### `POST /craft`
472	
473	Finds a crafting table within 16 blocks and goes to it if the item needs
474	one.
475	
476	```powershell
477	curl.exe -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3201/craft `
478	  -H "Content-Type: application/json" `
479	  -d '{"item":"wooden_pickaxe","amount":1}'
480	```
481	
482	Body: `{item, amount?=1}`.
483	
484	### `POST /chat`
485	
486	```powershell
487	curl.exe -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3201/chat `
488	  -H "Content-Type: application/json" `
489	  -d '{"message":"heading out to chop wood"}'
490	```
491	
492	Body: `{message, style?}`. `style` defaults to `"talk"`, which now
493	auto-classifies via the runner's `smartChat` — see Chat tiers above:
494	`!`-prefixed and protocol-ledger-prefixed (`TRADE `/`USING `/
495	`FREE `/`LEASE-BREAK `/`BASE `/`CLAIM `/`HELLO `/`OFFER `) lines go out
496	as real white chat verbatim, everything else becomes grey narration
497	automatically (`DEPOT ` included since 2026-09-01 — see Chat tiers).
498	Pass `"style":"status"` to force grey, `"fancy"` for a
499	gold accent, or `"rainbow"` for a tribe-wide proclamation.
500	
501	### `POST /autoeat`
502	
503	```powershell
504	curl.exe -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3201/autoeat `
505	  -H "Content-Type: application/json" `
506	  -d '{"on":true}'
507	```
508	
509	Body: `{on: boolean}`. Returns `204` with a note in the body if the
510	`mineflayer-auto-eat` plugin isn't loaded on this runner.
511	
512	### `POST /stop`
513	
514	Cancels whatever the bot is currently doing, cleanly. No body needed.
515	
516	```powershell
517	curl.exe -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3201/stop
518	```
519	
520	### `POST /eval`
521	
522	Escape hatch. Runs your `code` as the body of an async function with
523	`(bot, mcData, skills, log)` in scope; return a JSON-safe value.
524	
525	```powershell
526	curl.exe -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3201/eval `
527	  -H "Content-Type: application/json" `
528	  -d '{"code":"return { pos: bot.entity.position, held: bot.heldItem?.name };"}'
529	```
530	
531	Body: `{code}`. Errors come back as `{"error": "..."}` rather than
532	throwing across the HTTP boundary. There's a 10s soft timeout — if your
533	code is still running past that, the response will note it's still in
534	flight rather than blocking forever. Use this for anything the fixed
535	skills don't cover, and remember the escalation rule above: if you had to
536	reach for `/eval` because a skill failed twice, report it.
537	
538	### `GET /events?since=<n>`
539	
540	Ring buffer (last 500) of notable events: chat heard, health drops,
541	death, kicked, task transitions, quirk hits.
542	
543	```powershell
544	curl.exe -s "http://127.0.0.1:3201/events?since=0"
545	```
546	
547	Response: `{"events":[{"seq":1,"ts":"...","type":"chat","msg":"..."}],
548	"last":42}`. Pass the last `seq` you've seen as `since` next time to get
549	only what's new.
550	
551	## HOME SYSTEM (self-rescue)
552	
553	A server-side datapack (`cavehome`, installed in the world's
554	`datapacks/` folder — not part of this repo) gives every player two
555	legit `/trigger` commands, no admin involvement needed:
556	
557	- `/trigger sethome` — saves the runner's current position as *their
558	  own* home. Per-player automatically (scoreboard-backed, keyed by
559	  username — 8+ bots sharing the server each get their own home, no
560	  collision).
561	- `/trigger home` — teleports the runner back to their saved home. If
562	  no home was ever set, it sends a grey hint instead of erroring:
563	  `[cavehome] no home set yet - run /trigger sethome first.`
564	
565	Drive it exactly like any other chat command, through `/eval` (not
566	`/chat`, since `/trigger` is a raw slash-command, not a talk line):
567	
568	```powershell
569	curl.exe -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3201/eval `
570	  -H "Content-Type: application/json" `
571	  -d '{"code":"bot.chat(\"/trigger sethome\")"}'
572	```
573	
574	```powershell
575	curl.exe -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3201/eval `
576	  -H "Content-Type: application/json" `
577	  -d '{"code":"bot.chat(\"/trigger home\")"}'
578	```
579	
580	**Doctrine:**
581	
582	1. **Set home at the camp yard** — around **(12, 93, 50)** — on spawn
583	   and whenever you're back at camp for a while. A stale home (deep in
584	   a mine you've since left) is still safer to return to than nowhere,
585	   but refresh it when you can.
586	2. **Try the FEEDBACK.md stuck-taxonomy self-rescues first** — the
587	   wedge-detection nuisance-block clear, a `/stop` + re-`/goto`, digging
588	   out by hand via `/eval`. `/trigger home` is the **escalation**, not
589	   the first move, for a bot that's step-snagged, full-wedged, or sealed
590	   in a pocket it can't path or dig out of in reasonable time.
591	3. **This replaces orchestrator/RCON teleports**, which are now BANNED
592	   (see the superseded tp-rescue policy above) — the bot rescues
593	   *itself* with a command any regular player can run, not an admin
594	   backdoor.
595	4. Still narrate it in chat and report the stuck condition per the
596	   Escalation rule — `/trigger home` gets you out, it doesn't excuse
597	   skipping the report that gets the underlying pathing bug fixed.
598	
599	Live-tested round trip on TestRock (2026-09-01): home saved at
600	`(18.97, 102, 120.92)`, bot walked/displaced ~12 blocks to
601	`(24.66, 103.42, 131.70)`, `/trigger home` returned it to
602	`(18.95, 102, 120.93)` — within 0.02 blocks of the saved home.
603	
604	## More info
605	
606	- Port registry, roster, naming scheme, base location, goal ladder:
607	  `CIV.md`.
608	- What `cave/` is and how to start/stop bots from outside the runner:
609	  `README.md`.
